**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 7.7 (p0032)**

Section 7.7 requires *Customer* to pay Vendor "as liquidated damages and not as a penalty" 15% of annual Fees **for each week** an invoice is unpaid, triggered by a mere ten-day delay. This compounds to more than the full annual contract value in roughly seven weeks and is triggered by a minor breach — squarely walk-away territory, and failing both the preferred position (no Customer-payable LDs) and the fallback (single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees).

I confirmed there are no other Customer-payable stipulated amounts: Section 9.4 permits termination without cause with only accrued Fees owed (plus refund of prepayments), and Section 27 confirms termination without penalty on prolonged force majeure. Service credits flowing to us were not flagged.

Redline (validated, preferred level): replace the liquidated damages mechanic with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts as Vendor's sole remedy, plus an express statement that Customer bears no liquidated damages or penalties under the Agreement.
